name: ACCRINT
description: ACCRINT returns the accrued interest from the issue date to the settlement date for a bond or other fixed-income security.
tldr: Calculates accrued interest for a security that pays periodic interest.

parameters.name: first_interest
parameters.description: Date of the first interest payment.

parameters.name: settlement
parameters.description: Date the security is sold to the buyer.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Number of coupon payments per year (1, 2, or 4).

parameters.name: calc_method
parameters.description: TRUE = calculated from issue date (default), FALSE = from first_interest.

basicExample.description: Accrued interest for a semi-annual bond
basicExample.explanation: Calculates accrued interest from January 1 to April 1 for a 5% semi-annual bond with $1,000 par value.

advancedExamples.title: Accrued interest with actual/365 day count
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 3 counts actual days and uses a 365-day year.

howItWorks: ACCRINT calculates the interest that has accumulated since the last coupon payment. The result is based on the coupon rate, par value, and the number of days between the issue date and settlement date.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Dates must be entered as valid Excel dates or with the DATE function.
Different basis values produce different day-count results.

commonErrors.fix: Verify dates are valid and frequency/basis are correct.

commonErrors.cause: Dates are not recognized as dates.
commonErrors.fix: Use DATE(year, month, day) or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ACCRINT works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is accrued interest?
faq.answer: Accrued interest is the interest earned but not yet paid since the last coupon date.

faq.question: What is the default par value in ACCRINT?
faq.answer: The default par value is $1,000 if omitted in some implementations, but Excel requires it.
